newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off on cabinet shake-up rumor.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off on cabinet shake-up rumor.

text.p: Cracks appeared in the edifice of Venezuela's recent economic confidence as stocks slipped on rumors of a shake-up in the economic cabinet and the possible resignation of Planing Minister Teodoro Petkoff, analysts said.
"It shows just how fragile the country's confidence is," said Merinvest analyst Boris Molina.
The bolsa's 19-share index closed off 1.98 percent at 6,023.55 despite categorical denials by both Petkoff and President Rafael Caldera's office that the economic cabinet would not change.
"Today's market began strong and looked to rise," Molina said. "But sell orders started coming in as soon as foreign investors started worrying about Petkoff."
Molina said that local confidence was further dented by recent congressional questioning of the slated November sale of the government's 49 percent share in telephone company CANTV.
Among traded issues, 33 fell, seven closed flat and five rose as a total of 23 million shares traded worth 4.5 billion dollars ($9.6 million).

Bellwether stock Electricidad de Caracas lost 13.90 bolivars to end at 538.10, steel-maker Sivensa lost 13.00 bolivars to end at 362.00, while foods producer Mavesa slipped 1.00 bolivar to close at 151.00.
